speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Most of the patients have recovered and are no longer symptomatic.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Although we had been expecting it, many Singaporeans were concerned when Zika cases first emerged in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Their anxiety is understandable, given that Zika is little known here.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have learnt much over the last two weeks.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Allow me to give the House an update on the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The first documented case of Zika was in Africa in 1947.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The first reported large outbreak occurred in 2007, in Micronesia.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Zika was unknown in the Americas until last year when a number of cases were reported in north-eastern Brazil.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: By now, 72 countries and territories have reported evidence of Zika virus transmission.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Zika is transmitted via the Aedes mosquito, which can also carry the dengue and chikungunya viruses.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Zika can also be spread through sexual transmission in some cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: About four out of five persons infected with the Zika virus will not have symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The rest will only have mild symptoms, which include fever and rash, and other symptoms such as red eyes and joint pain.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On rare occasions, patients may also develop Guillain-Barré Syndrome, a disease that temporarily affects the nervous system.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Zika is, however, of concern among pregnant women.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: A small number of babies born to pregnant women with Zika infection may develop microcephaly, a congenital condition that affects the development of the brain.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Research is still ongoing to better understand the association between Zika and microcephaly.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had expected Zika to come to Singapore sooner or later, given the large volume of travel in and out of Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We prepared for Zika on a few fronts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: First, the Ministry of Health (MOH) worked with the National Environment Agency's (NEA's) Environmental Health Institute to put in place a sentinel surveillance programme for Zika two years ago.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We partnered about 200 clinics island-wide to collect blood samples from selected patients with symptoms associated with Zika, which are quite similar to dengue, and tested them for the Zika virus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Close to 4,000 samples were tested between February Page: 48 and August, before the first confirmed case happened.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: At the same time, we strengthened our laboratory capabilities to facilitate the testing and management of patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a second layer of defence, we kept our doctors, especially our general practitioners (GPs), abreast of the developments on Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Our GPs are the first line of care for most Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They have been helpful in alerting us to unusual disease patterns.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We have also made Zika a notifiable disease under the Infectious Diseases Act from January this year, so that MOH would immediately be alerted if any doctor or laboratory in Singapore detects a case of Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Third, we sought to reduce the risk of importation of Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We issued travel advice to outbound travellers to Zika-affected areas and inbound travellers returning from these areas.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Fourth, we stepped up public education and issued health advisories.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In early February, we set up the Clinical Advisory Group on Zika and Pregnancy, to develop a health advisory for pregnant women, and also to advise doctors on the clinical management of pregnant women with Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: An interim clinical guidance was issued in mid-April.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Fifth, we strengthened our operational readiness for an outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In January this year, MOH worked with partner agencies to prepare our operational plans in case of an outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In July, we conducted a multi-agency exercise where we simulated the import of an infectious disease into Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This exercise involved a wide range of partner agencies, including the Ministry of Trade and Industry and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM).

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Meanwhile, we continued to monitor global developments related to Zika closely to obtain regular updates on the situation worldwide.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On 13 May, he tested positive for Zika, and the patient was quickly isolated at the Communicable Diseases Centre (CDC) at Tan Tock Seng Hospital.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We screened the patient's household members, and NEA deployed a larger team of officers to conduct intensive vector control operations in the area around his home in Watten Estate.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Residents in the area were given Zika information leaflets and were advised to seek medical attention should they develop symptoms of fever and rash.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We also asked the clinics in the vicinity to look out for Zika-like symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The man was discharged after he tested negative for the Zika virus and recovered.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: No other cases were subsequently linked to this case and the virus was successfully contained.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Three months later, in the evening of 22 August, MOH was alerted by a GP from the Sims Drive Medical Clinic on an unusual increase in cases of fever, rash and joint pain that had tested negative for dengue and chikungunya.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The next day, MOH arranged with the GP to refer new cases with similar symptoms to the CDC.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: On 25 August, that is, two days after, we approached the supervisor of a nearby construction site for records of workers who had recently been unwell, so that they could be investigated further.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Page: 49 Following this, we alerted the GPs in the Aljunied Crescent and Sims Drive area to specifically look out for patients with Zika-like symptoms, and advised residents in the area to see their doctors if they had such symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NEA also intensified vector control operations in the vicinity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: By now, MOH and NEA have moved beyond the surveillance phase, to actively detect cases and identify clusters to manage the spread of Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To determine the extent and the locations of the spread, we not only looked out for new cases, but also looked backwards in time to investigate past cases in the vicinity.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As a number of such cases were construction workers, we went back to the construction site on 27 August to trace and test workers who had recently recovered from fever, and also assessed and tested new patients.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This sudden jump was surprising to some people, who wondered if these cases had, in fact, been detected earlier but held back by MOH.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In reality, the number of confirmed new Zika-positive patients – and I repeat – new Zika-positive patients, increased only by five.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The other 36 were from our proactive back-tracing of workers at the construction site.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many of them have already recovered from the sickness.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Through the back-tracing, we also checked the onset of symptoms to determine the epidemiology of the outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Some people misinterpreted this as MOH having known of the first Zika-positive case since 31 July.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As I explained, we only confirmed the first locally transmitted Zika case on 27 August, and we released the information the same evening.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We subsequently identified new clusters beyond Aljunied and Sims Drive and we provided updates daily.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked how we manage construction sites and dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOM and NEA have stepped up the engagement of construction sites and dormitory operators to intensify their vector control efforts to prevent mosquito breeding.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOM has also reminded employers and dormitory operators to encourage workers to seek medical attention and notify their supervisors, should they feel unwell.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Measures such as temperature taking have limited effect for Zika since a majority of infected individuals are asymptomatic, that is, they do not run a temperature.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As Zika is a mosquito-borne disease, the key strategy is vector control.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I would also like to assure Assoc Prof Daniel Goh that our primary healthcare system is accessible to foreign workers, should they need to see a doctor.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The cost of their treatment will be borne by their employers.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As more cases and clusters emerge, our efforts are focused on vector control.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Isolation of patients has limited effect as 80% of those with Zika are asymptomatic, that means they have no symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Hospitalisation of Zika patients is also not necessary as we have found that most cases have mild symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Patients will be hospitalised Page: 50 only if it is clinically necessary.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We had also reviewed our policy on the testing of suspect cases.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Initially, we were focused on the clusters in order to quickly assess the nature and extent of the outbreak to guide our strategy.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We therefore provided free testing for those with symptoms who lived, worked or studied in the areas that were affected.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: As more cases were found in other parts of Singapore, we extended Zika testing beyond the clusters and now provide a subsidy to all Singaporeans with Zika-like symptoms at the public healthcare institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Many pregnant women are understandably anxious about Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We are paying particular attention to them because of the possible risks to their foetuses if they are infected by Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Clinical Advisory Group for Zika and Pregnancy had, on 30 August, updated its guidelines on the health advisory, testing and clinical management for pregnant women.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: These were aligned with WHO guidelines which advise that Zika testing for asymptomatic pregnant women is not routinely recommended.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: However, WHO's guidelines do recommend testing for symptomatic pregnant women and those whose male partners had tested positive for Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Symptomatic pregnant women and those whose male partners have tested positive should seek the advice of their doctors.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They will be provided with free Zika tests at both public and private healthcare institutions if their doctors assess that testing is needed.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Regular ultrasound scans will be carried out to monitor the development of the foetus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Zika infection does not always result in abnormal foetal development.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: It is, therefore, important that pregnant women be appropriately advised and monitored by the relevant specialists.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Babies born with microcephaly will be supported and cared for, just as we do for babies with other congenital conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Mr Png Eng Huat asked how we could raise public awareness of Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Public awareness is one of the most critical elements in our fight against Zika and we have undertaken multiple efforts on this front.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since January this year, we have kept the public updated on Zika developments through the media and the MOH website, providing information on precautions to take when travelling to Zika-affected areas.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Since 27 August, we have shared information with the media and the public on a daily basis.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) has set up a microsite on Zika with useful and easy-to-read infographics and videos on "What is Zika?", providing advice to pregnant women, as well as the latest updates on the Zika situation in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MCI has also produced some interstitials on Zika, which have been broadcast on free-to-air channels, starting from last week.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NEA has also set up a website with statistics on Zika infections and clusters.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: NEA, in Page: 51 collaboration with the grassroots organisations, has continued its outreach to the community through information leaflets and posters on Zika and dengue.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This has gone hand-in-hand with their vector control operations.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: In Chua Chu Kang, for example, with the support of NEA, students from Pioneer Junior College and the Institute of Technical Education College West, grassroots leaders and volunteers, we visited 134 blocks in my constituency on 4 September, to share with residents information on Zika and what they can do.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: And I am sure many other Members have done the same.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I have no doubt that we will be able to learn more about the Zika virus through global and local research efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We cannot tell at this moment whether the viruses found here cause more or less severe disease than those in South America.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Further research will be needed to shed light on this.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We can also expect more test kits to be on the market in future.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: They will need to undergo field trials, be validated by laboratory professionals, and approved by regulators to ensure they are safe, and the results are reliable before they are available for use.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Currently, there is no specific anti-viral treatment or approved vaccine for Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Early-stage human trials have commenced for experimental vaccines.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: There are also ongoing research efforts in Singapore on Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: But testing and translating these to practical clinical use will take time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Mr Alex Yam asked whether the Ministry will consider setting up a National Zika Registry.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Meanwhile, we are already tracking Zika, which is a notifiable disease.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Microcephaly has been tracked by the National Birth Defects Registry since January 1993.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: We will work with our doctors to monitor the outcomes of babies born to women with Zika over time.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mdm Speaker, most people infected with the Zika virus will only have mild symptoms and can recover without treatment.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Doctors will provide counselling to pregnant women who tested positive for Zika and closely monitor the development of the foetus.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH has been working closely with NEA to intensity vector control and eradicate mosquito breeding grounds.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: To further reduce the risk of transmission of Zika, we must take a whole-of-society approach in our fight against Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Each one of us also has a part to play.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I believe that as long as we work together, we can win the battle against Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: (In English): Let me continue to conclude in English.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Page: 52 First, it is important to be transparent and timely in sharing accurate information.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This is why we released regular updates on Zika, in order to keep the public apprised of the situation.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: This also prevents rumours and untruths from spreading and creating confusion and suspicion.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: MOH and the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources are grateful that we have had strong support from our healthcare partners and professionals, Government agencies such as NEA, MCI, MOM and PA, in responding to this outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Lastly, but even more importantly, a whole-of-Government approach is still not enough.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Even as NEA continues its vector control efforts, each one of us should do what we can to reduce the spread of Zika by taking personal precautions against mosquitoes and checking for mosquito breeding in our homes and our workplaces.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: I urge all Singaporeans to continue to remain vigilant and do our part, to protect Singapore against Zika.

speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
text: Therefore, as we tackle Zika, life must go on.

speaker: Mdm Speaker
text: As the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will be making a related Statement, I will take all clarifications after that Statement has been delivered.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I will now highlight the mosquito control measures my Ministry and NEA have undertaken to control the mosquito population prior to and during the outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As everyone knows by now, Zika and dengue are conveyed by the same mosquito – the Aedes aegypti.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our key strategy for dengue control, and now Zika, is source reduction – the detection and removal of breeding habitats and larvae.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This integrated vector management strategy is in line with WHO's recommendations and remains especially critical now, as we are in the traditional dengue peak season.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Using a risk-based approach in NEA's vector control, our officers conduct pre-emptive checks and vector control efforts as precautionary measures in areas identified with high Aedes mosquito population.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When a dengue or Zika cluster is identified, we intensify our source eradication efforts by partnering the community and premise owners to eliminate mosquito breeding habitats.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Page: 53 Fogging is also conducted to kill the mosquitos as an additional measure to quickly curtail the transmission of dengue or Zika.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Following the Zika outbreak, we have heard calls for fogging to be conducted at various residential estates.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Currently, NEA carries out indoor spraying of insecticides and outdoor fogging or misting to kill adult mosquitoes in the Zika clusters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is the same thing we do in the dengue clusters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These measures are helpful in the clusters because they have infected adult mosquitoes which must be destroyed before they bite and infect more people.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, it would not be wise to conduct fogging indiscriminately outside of the clusters as a preventive measure.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This means that fogging will have to be repeated frequently as new batches of mosquitoes continue to emerge from breeding habitats that are not removed.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Routine fogging is not a sustainable vector control measure.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thirdly, the overuse or indiscriminate use of chemical treatment may cause the build-up of resistance in the local mosquito population.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Fogging should only be used when there are Zika or dengue clusters or when the adult mosquito population is observed to be high so that we can mitigate the situation quickly and, again, I qualify, it is only effective when worked together with source eradication.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I just read an article in The Economist where experts fighting the same Aedes aegypti mosquito in Florida have come to the same conclusion that fogging on its own is not effective and that the only real solution is, in fact, "boots on the ground".

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And this is the best way to destroy the breeding habitats.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given that this particular mosquito, the Aedes aegypti, likes to be around humans, lives in crowded places, and lay eggs in clean water, the only way to mitigate the risk of dengue or Zika is to prevent the mosquito from emerging in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Indeed, human blood is needed by the female Aedes mosquitoes to lay eggs and breed.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They will go everywhere where there is human blood to feed on and water to breed their offspring.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why our NEA officers' boots have been on the ground for years to eradicate breeding spots in accessible and public areas.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why we have to emphasise repeatedly that every household must also constantly do the necessary ground actions to remove potential breeding spots in their own homes where it is not easily accessible to our officers.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Historically, we notice a change in the predominant virus is usually followed by a spike in dengue cases.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thirdly, a large proportion of our population lacks immunity to dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases as a result of intensive mosquito control in the past decades.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In many other countries where dengue is endemic, the affected are often children.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is not the case in Singapore, which is good.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our success has, therefore, and however, paradoxically lowered our herd immunity so that disease transmission occurs easily even with a very small mosquito population.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Page: 54 Fourthly, our region's constantly warm climate and high humidity allow the mosquitoes to breed all year round.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The warmer climate also supports faster breeding and the maturation cycle of the mosquitoes, which contribute to a higher population and the spread of diseases.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This specific mosquito, as I have mentioned, has adapted particularly well to our urban environment because it loves human beings, compared to animals, and likes to breed, mate and feed near human dwellings.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We must acknowledge that all these extraneous factors make it impossible to eliminate the Aedes aegypti here.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Indeed, if we had done anything less, dengue and Zika would have spread throughout the whole island more quickly and thoroughly.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Therefore, we are far from helpless and can do much to mitigate the risks.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These Gravitraps will allow us to identify areas with a large Aedes aegypti population and take targeted mosquito control measures proactively even if there are no dengue or Zika cases.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This sort of risk-based, preventive surveillance work will go on well ahead of any peak transmission season.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng has asked for the number of site checks conducted by NEA and the proportion of mosquito breeding habitats found.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Besides conducting preventive surveillance, we inspect all the premises and public areas within the cluster, conduct indoor spraying of insecticides and outdoor fogging to kill adult mosquitoes, as well as oiling of breeding habitats to kill any mosquito larvae.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the construction sites, we have stepped up enforcement actions and penalties over the years in addition to imposing fines.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 1998, we passed the Control of Vectors and Pesticides Act (CVPA) which allows us to impose Stop Work Orders (SWO) for worksites repeatedly found with poor housekeeping and mosquito breeding habitats.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The number of SWOs imposed on errant sites increased from 2013 as a result of a tightened regime.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Since 1999, NEA has required all construction sites exceeding $50 million in project value to employ full-time Environmental Control Officers (ECO) while sites between $10 million and $50 million are required to employ part-time ones.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Page: 55 While NEA has given attention to construction sites, I must reiterate that a large number of mosquito breeding sites is, in fact, still found in homes.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Earlier this year, given the potentially large number of dengue cases as well as the impending threat of Zika, the NEA renewed the call for everyone to safeguard our own home.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While the current strategy has kept the mosquito population here low, we are exploring new methods to further tackle the mosquito problem.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I recently announced plans to trial a novel method of suppressing the mosquito population through the release of male Aedes aegypti mosquitos carrying Wolbachia to mate with wild female Wolbachia-free Aedes mosquitos.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Eggs produced from the mating between the male Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquito and a wild female Aedes aegypti mosquito will not hatch.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The trial follows a four-year intensive study and comprehensive risk assessments by NEA's Environment Health Institute, and support shown by the WHO, the United States (US), Australia, and so on.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: From October 2016, male Wolbachia-carrying Aedes aegypti mosquitos will be released in three selected sites.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: If successful, this will complement our existing mosquito control efforts and eventually lead to the suppression of the Aedes aegypti mosquito population and a possible curtailment of dengue or Zika transmission.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That said, the Wolbachia technology is not a silver bullet.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will take some years before we can deploy it at scale.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And with or without this kind of breakthrough, I want to stress that everyone must still continue with source reduction efforts.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our mosquito control strategy has helped us to suppress dengue over the years and I will now address the questions raised by Mr Christopher de Souza, Mr Dennis Tan and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, to show that this same strategy has prepared us well to tackle our Zika challenge now.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Following MOH's announcement of the first locally transmitted Zika case on 27 August 2016, we immediately alerted the 27 members of our Inter-Agency Dengue Taskforce.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Every day, around 300 NEA officers, contractors and volunteers carry out vector control efforts and outreach in these clusters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As of 11 September 2016, more than 31,000 premises in the various Zika clusters have been inspected for mosquito breeding.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: More than 200 mosquito breedings have been detected and destroyed in the clusters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the Zika clusters, thermal fogging outdoors and indoor spraying of premises have been carried out to kill adult mosquitoes and the drains have been flushed to remove any stagnant water as an added precaution.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At this point, I would like to thank the residents in the Zika clusters for their show of support and cooperation to our officers.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They willingly opened up their homes for our officers to do their inspections and helpfully pointed out areas of concern to them for action.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Again, we need everyone to step up and forward to help take good care of our homes and neighbourhoods so that we can all maintain good health.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: NEA has also inspected the construction sites and workers' dormitories in the Zika clusters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: An SWO was issued to the construction site at Sims Drive on 27 August 2016 to curtail the local Zika transmission as the site had failed to maintain satisfactory housekeeping and to eliminate potential mosquito breeding habitats.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Page: 56 NEA has, in fact, been working regularly with the Singapore Contractors Association (SCAL) and Senior Minister of State Amy Khor recently met them again to drive home the point that their construction site supervisors would need to be more vigilant about mosquito control and to look out for any workers with Zika symptoms.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Communication is key in any public health situation.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together with MOH, we have provided updates of our efforts and actions through the daily media briefings.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Up-to-date information on the Zika clusters has been put up on the NEA website since last Wednesday.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have also engaged our community partners to conduct extensive outreach to the residents in the Zika clusters.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Over the past two weekends, outreach activities supporting the Mozzie Wipeout Movement Against Zika were conducted all over Singapore to remove stagnant water in common areas, dispose of discarded receptacles properly, and distribute Zika information leaflets to the residents.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Contractors and dormitory operators, please maintain proper housekeeping.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Town Councils, please help eliminate potential breeding sites in the common areas and undertake fogging sensibly.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is our insurance against a widespread outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us all continue together to keep our boots on the ground, keep calm and carry on.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   We are on the right track.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our strategy of rigorous mosquito control and our well-coordinated public education efforts have been commended by WHO as well as the US' Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Everyone – the Sovernment agencies, premises owners, businesses, residents, the community – has a role in our fight against dengue and Zika.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For home owners, let us continue to perform the steps to "Do the Mozzie Wipeout".

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the contractors and dormitory operators, please maintain proper housekeeping at the building sites and dormitories.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For the Town Councils, please help to eliminate the potential breeding sites in the common areas and undertake fogging sensibly.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: All these efforts are our insurance against a widespread outbreak.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us all continue to keep our boots on the ground, keep calm and carry on in our fight against this disease.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister of the Environment and Water Resources.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, would the Minister consider more stringent measures, such as introducing a new regime requiring all construction contractors, large and small, to engage authorised pest controllers to conduct independent checks and treatments at the construction sites?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Under this arrangement, the Government could spell out specific maintenance and housekeeping standards that all contractors must abide by or risk suspension of their operations until they comply.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: All construction sites would need to display clearance reports by these independent pest controllers at the construction sites so that the public can see that they have got a very systematic regime, and it is conducted by independent controllers, something like what was implemented by the Building and Construction Authority on the lift maintenance scheme.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think, firstly, we should not go overboard by implementing more measures and also adding more costs when we can do things well publicly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Again, I would like to stress the importance of having the support of all the premises owners, including construction site supervisors, so that they do not let their eyes off the ball.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Sometimes, there are dry seasons; the rain may not fall and, therefore, there may not be any mosquitoes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But the Aedes aegypti mosquito can breed any time of the year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we must never let our vigilance down.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, we must continue to work with them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And if these actions are not sufficient, if WHO or other experts tell us to do other things that will help us to fight it, we will definitely take it up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Please also allow me to place on record my appreciation to the MOH and NEA officers for their hard work on the ground since the start of the Zika infection.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Page: 58 A couple of questions for MOH.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: First of all, are we able to ascertain, at this point, the origin of this particular local transmission?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Were these patients informed that they were Zika-positive and was this particular exercise helpful in reducing the spread of Zika further?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: On microcephaly which is perhaps the most visual and the most frightening aspect of Zika, are there any other causes of microcephaly in babies and how many non-Zika microcephaly cases have there been in Singapore since the tracking began in 1993?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Also, in terms of public awareness that both the Ministers spoke about, have both the Ministries ascertained what the level of public awareness on Zika is at this moment, and what more can the Government do to stress the whole-of-society approach to containing Zika and preventing vector breeding?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last of all, a question for the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: First, Mr Alex Yam asked about the origin of the local transmission.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I presume he is asking about the first case locally.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is very difficult to determine the first case of Zika because Zika is not transmitted from person to person.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: From epidemiological studies, it is very difficult to trace who passes on to who because there is an intermediary factor and, that is, the mosquito.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are unable to trace the mosquito for obvious reasons.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we do not know who is the first so-called index case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We also have to be quite careful not to identify the person with the earliest onset of symptoms on 31 July as the first case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It may well not be because, again, 80% of the patients actually do not have symptoms.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is not necessary that the first person with symptoms is the first case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I hope I have addressed the Member's question.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, the answer is we do not really know who the index case in this outbreak is.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The look-back exercise was important to us in order to have a sense of how wide the cluster was and how many patients were involved, to allow us to determine very quickly rather than to have to wait for further cases to be investigated, and to size up the situation.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We decided to look back to allow us to have a quick assessment of the size of the cluster and to also allow NEA to focus its efforts where it matters.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For patients who are tested positive, we do inform them.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And for those who are still symptomatic, we isolated them in the beginning, as I had explained earlier.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They were hospitalised for us to observe them, as we wanted to be sure that they did not have complications either.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: By the time of the look-back, in fact, most of the patients in the look-back exercise had already recovered.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They were no longer symptomatic because, in the look-back exercise, we looked quite far backwards and many of them had already recovered.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We were just approaching them and asking them whether they were ill before, what their symptoms were and when their symptoms started.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is how we did the look-back exercise.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On microcephaly, Zika is not the only cause of microcephaly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Microcephaly can be due to a number of factors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It could be due to genetic and environmental factors, such as Down Syndrome, exposure to drugs and alcohol, rubella, as well as other infectious diseases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Even before we encountered the first case of Zika, microcephaly cases were present in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For Page: 59 these patients with microcephaly, we continue to provide support and manage them in the same way as we manage children with congenital conditions.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Mr Alex Yam also asked about the level of public awareness.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Those of us who have done home visits would know that the level of awareness is very high among the public.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Every door that we knock on, I always tell them, "I want to remind you about Zika." They will say, "Yah, Zika I heard of it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I watched the TV." Most of them are aware of Zika.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: And we will continue to raise public awareness.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Because research on this is still on-going, our knowledge of Zika is still very limited, in terms of scientific knowledge.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: There will be new discoveries and developments, and we need to continue to engage the public and keep them informed of these new developments.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First of all, because part of MacPherson was part of the first general cluster, I would like to also thank MOH, NEA, the Town Councils, pest control workers and grassroots leaders for their relentless efforts in the anti-Mozzie and anti-Zika efforts.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First of all, I would like to ask if Zika is now considered endemic in Singapore and if a full eradication is even possible.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Second, I note that WHO has praised Singapore and that we have also complied with the guidelines, in terms of how we can support and advise pregnant women in Singapore, I am wondering if more help can be given to them.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Until there is greater research and clarity in whether the local strain of Zika will cause more or less damage, in terms of pregnant women and the foetuses, I believe pregnant women will continue to be worried throughout the months of pregnancy.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: So, would regular tests be made available to all pregnant women during the pregnancy?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: And for those who have exhibited symptoms and tested positive, would MOH subsidise the expected increase in cost, given the anticipated increase in scans and other follow-ups needed to ensure the well-being of the foetuses?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Thirdly, is the current testing capacity enough to deal with the demand in case of a national outbreak again – hopefully not – and whether there is a need to increase the capacity for testing?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: This is especially so, given that mosquitoes are considered endemic in the tropical countries like ours?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is actually not productive for us to discuss on terminology, whether it is endemic or otherwise.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our immediate task is to focus on vector control, do our level best, try to eradicate as much as we can and, if not, to minimise as much as we can.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is our immediate task, and we should focus on this.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: I certainly hope that Zika will not be endemic.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: But it is something that we will have to monitor over a longer period of time before we can make a definitive assessment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: You have to test them while they are infected.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: After a period of time, when their infection has recovered, it will be very difficult to detect whether the lady has been infected before.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, the window is very narrow, Page: 60 and it is not practical to keep testing the lady every day, every week, or every other week.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: WHO did not recommend regular testing for those who are non-symptomatic.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Our Clinical Advisory Group also advised against it.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: For symptomatic pregnant women, the advice is for them to consult their doctors because each case is different, their risk factors are also different.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, it is better for them to consult their doctors.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: How often they need to be tested and monitored, their doctors will be able to advise them accordingly.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Ms Tin also asked about the additional cost.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they are subsidised patients, and if they are unable to afford the cost, especially for the lower-income families, MediFund is available for them, whether for the test or the treatment.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: On research funding, it is an area that we are also interested in.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It is something that we are discussing with the researchers and if they have worthwhile projects, they can put these up to NMRC, and we will support them accordingly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have three questions, two for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The first one is whether the 36 construction workers were discovered to be infected in the look-back exercise, whether they went to a clinic and, if they did, why were the clinics not able to detect an uptrend in the Zika symptoms and report that to MOH?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The second question is: what processes are in place to ensure construction site contractors would report large numbers of workers who display symptoms of dengue or Zika infection to MOH in a timely manner and, if none exists, whether there should be such processes?

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources, whether, other than size, the location of construction sites should be considered for more stringent surveillance, namely, how close the sites are to residential areas?

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, very often, the clinics may not be able to identify them as having potential Zika infection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Members would remember that I had explained how we identified the first case.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: It was because of a GP clinic that had identified a large number of patients with similar symptoms, and they were not able to determine the cause of the symptoms.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They had tested the patients for dengue and chikungunya, and they were not able to determine what infection the patients had.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: As I had also explained in my reply, our primary care system is, in fact, on the frontline of our surveillance.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: They are more sensitive because they are trained and on the lookout for unusual trends.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If they identity trends like what I mentioned earlier, they will alert us and then, we would go Page: 61 in and investigate.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: In addition to the GP network that we work with to identify unusual trends, we also have a sentinel surveillance system, where we work with partner GPs and our polyclinics to monitor and test selected samples regularly to ensure that even if they have no significant symptoms, if we are not able to determine the cause of the symptoms, we also test them for Zika to make sure that we are able to identify Zika infections if it is transmitted in the community.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Most of the clinics, when they do testing, under normal circumstances, the focus is on imported cases as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, if they see symptoms that resemble Zika, even if they are light symptoms, they would check the travel history.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: If the patient has been to Zika-infected countries, then alarm will be raised.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That is also part of the system to track imported cases.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: That was how the first case in Watten Estate was discovered, because he had a travel history to Brazil.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When he returned, we discovered that he had symptoms.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Therefore, we sent his blood for testing, and we discovered Zika that way.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: The Member's second question on a large number of patients in the construction sites, again, as I had explained, the key gatekeeper is our primary care system.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We work through our GPs when they notice unusual trends, whether it is Zika or any other infection.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: We are on the lookout not just for Zika but also other potential infectious diseases, including diseases that we may not be aware of as well.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, our frontline GPs are the most important.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: When they see cases that they have doubts about, or when they see patterns that are unusual which they cannot explain, they will usually alert MOH, and we will work together with them to find out the truth.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: This was how we discovered a locally transmitted case in the first instance.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the question of whether we should focus more on construction areas near residential sites, Singapore is a very built-up area.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, it is not the primary factor why we go to that site or not.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And now, indeed, we have extended the coverage to beyond the construction sites to the dormitories where the workers come from.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Regarding what the Minister said about the male Wolbachia mosquito experiment, what is the expected time frame for this experiment before the Ministry decides to introduce it on a bigger scale?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And I have one quick question for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In other areas, they just have to fly horizontally.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to know whether these mosquitoes will fly high and how high and whether they will survive long enough in our urban environment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, after six months, if successful – and I hope it is successful so that we do not have to recalibrate again – we can then deploy them across for small-scale study and field suppression trials.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And then if successful, we will roll it out for higher-risk areas.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Earlier on, I said that based on a study, more than 90% of people find it easy to find the information on Zika.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Actually, the survey was done by the feedback unit Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry @ Home, and not by MCI.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: Just now, Mr Dennis Tan asked about the strain of the current Zika virus in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, the strain that we have is an earlier generation, which means that it has been circulating in Asia even before Brazil had a Zika outbreak.

speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
text: So, this is the current strain that we have identified.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Also how effective is fogging and are there any side effects to fogging?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I mentioned in my Statement just now, fogging is effective if done properly, if done by a licensed professional.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have to fog when there is a cluster because it means that there are adult mosquitoes infecting the population or to prevent those mosquitoes which are not yet infecting from infecting.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, that is the primary reason why we do fogging.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I know everyone likes fogging because it is very visual, everyone can see it and everyone feels better, but it does not solve the problem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It must be done together with source eradication, whether it is a construction site or our homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Indeed, at our homes, whenever the fogging is done, they close up their homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And, therefore, it does not get into the homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The other thing we could do is misting, which means that in some Town Councils as well as dormitories, we do misting to make the chemical stick on the wall and it lasts longer.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But we cannot do this very often either.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As I mentioned just now, there are also side effects of using the same chemical over and over again so frequently that the mosquitoes may become immune to those insecticides.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In fact, some insecticides are not used at all nowadays because we have overused them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A word of caution for everybody and I am glad that, as I watched my phone, the headlines that are coming out are that there are many myths to fogging and we hope that we are doing accurate, better fogging than just more fogging.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The first relates to the Minister's answer just now on the number of venues where breeding sites were destroyed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The Minister said that half were in homes.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would the Minister be able to share in what other areas, besides these, can these sites of breeding be found?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Page: 63 The second question relates to a back-of-the-envelope calculation that I did, based on the figures the Minister provided.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: In light of this, would his Ministry consider taking an even more robust approach to stamping out mosquito breeding sites in construction sites, especially since my own Clementi residents have expressed concern every time a new construction site comes up nearby?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Anecdotally, I can share that, on walkabouts, my residents and I also find that we are more likely to get bitten by mosquitoes when we are near a construction site that has active construction activity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They just go to where there are humans and there is water to breed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And whether it is a construction site or a home, it should be of equal concern to us.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For construction sites, our officers can come in anytime.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: They can impose appropriate orders on them to clean up, put in the right officers, and step up on their housekeeping.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, even in terms of per home basis, we are actually far better than what has been prescribed by WHO.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Every mosquito that hatches, a female mosquito will hatch a further 300 eggs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, whether it is home or construction site, we must be as vigilant, and I think we also should educate our constituents that it is not just about the construction site.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will do our best to suppress the source of breeding if it occurs there.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But everyone must do their part to make sure they do the five "mozzie wipeout" steps as a daily habit to ensure that they do not give the mosquitoes a chance to breed.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, when asked to share their findings with the condominium managements, NEA rejected the request.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would NEA consider sharing such information so that it can be a community effort for follow-up action?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Like when they visit the homes, if they are found to have bred mosquitoes, can such information be shared with the condominium managements?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Even for public housing, our Housing and Development Board flats, we do not specify which unit exactly where the breeding happens.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: It is enough for the information that, in this particular building or block, that is a cluster, because there is more than one and there is a chance that it was infected by one or the other.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, it is enough for people to take heed and to know that some form of transmission is happening and take more precaution Page: 64 to go round their house to eradicate the source of breeding.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, I think it is not important to know the exact unit.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Everyone's role is to ensure that there is no breeding at home and then, if there are adult mosquitoes, particularly seen in large numbers in the condominium, to do the fogging as appropriate.
